title: Still life in a classic Blume-Capel model: pseudo-transitions in a spin-1 diamond chain
authors: Elham Shahhosseini Shahrabadi, Majid Moradi, Jozef Strecka
abstract: We exactly investigate the ground-state, magnetic, and thermodynamic properties of a spin-1 Blume-Capel diamond chain in a magnetic field by means of the transfer-matrix method. After establishing the complete ground-state phase diagram and characterizing each ground-state spin configuration, we examine the finite-temperature behavior in the vicinity of selected phase boundaries and triple points. It is demonstrated that an extremely small energy gap between a nondegenerate ground state and competing macroscopically degenerate low-lying excited states gives rise to entropically-driven pseudo-transitions. These pseudo-transitions manifest themselves through abrupt but continuous changes in the magnetization and entropy resembling discontinuous jumps, while the magnetic susceptibility and specific heat exhibit exceptionally sharp yet finite peaks resembling divergences. Our results provide the exact evidence that pseudo-transitions can also emerge in the classical spin-1 Blume-Capel model and thereby extend the class of one-dimensional spin systems known to display pseudo-transitions.
summary: This theoretical work uses the transfer-matrix method to study a spin-1 Blume-Capel diamond chain. The authors demonstrate that the system exhibits 'pseudo-transitions'—sharp, continuous crossovers rather than true phase transitions—when tuned near specific phase boundaries. This extends the known class of 1D systems displaying such entropy-driven anomalies.
main_problem: The study investigates pseudo-transitions—anomalous crossovers mimicking true phase transitions—in a one-dimensional spin system where such transitions are forbidden by theorems.
main_result: The paper provides exact evidence that these entropy-driven pseudo-transitions can occur in the classical spin-1 Blume-Capel model, characterized by abrupt changes in magnetization and sharp, finite peaks in susceptibility/specific heat.
method: The transfer-matrix method is employed to exactly calculate thermodynamic properties (partition function, free energy) for the system along its chain dimension.
model_or_system: The physical system is a spin-1 Blume-Capel diamond chain. The Hamiltonian involves interactions ($J_1, J_2$) and single-ion anisotropy ($D$), subjected to an external magnetic field ($h$).
key_observables: Magnetization (M), Entropy (S), Magnetic Susceptibility ($\chi$), and Specific Heat (C).
important_parameters: Interaction ratios ($J_2/J_1$), anisotropy ratio ($D/J_1$), external field ($h/J_1$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: Periodic boundary conditions are assumed for the chain structure; the pseudo-transition mechanism relies on thermal activation near macroscopically degenerate low-lying excited states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ground-state phase diagram showing entropy density, and temperature dependence plots demonstrating sharp crossovers in M, $\chi$, S, and C near pseudocritical temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Hamiltonian and uses the transfer-matrix method to determine the partition function. It then analyzes the ground-state phase diagram before examining finite-temperature behavior to pinpoint pseudo-transition signatures via thermodynamic observables.
why_interesting: While focused on classical spin models, the concept of entropy-driven crossovers mimicking quantum criticality is highly relevant for understanding crossover regimes in complex many-body systems studied in AMO physics.
